technical: The Java attach WARN lines quoted in the post don't match the raw evidence. The post shows pid=3886 and pid=4090, but the scanner recorded pid=388 and pid=409. Fix: Paste both lines verbatim from 05-fix.log:29 and :33. Keep the error= field if it is in the log, and don't edit pids or timestamps. If the scanner cut the pid short, quote the full log line and say so.

technical: A promised result is missing. The open question asks how many services share a trace across two nodes with and without header propagation. The default case returned 0 of 56 IDs within the 90-second wait, so there is no comparison. The contract still records services_in_trace_default as ok. Also, the load sets traceparent on the wire, so finding zero traces in the default case is a gap in what was read back, not a measured result. Fix: Rerun only the default trace case. Poll the trace API until the found count levels off (for example up to 5 minutes), or run the propagation case first, so both cases have the same chance of being indexed. Report joined of found for each case. Mark services_in_trace_default as not measured until it has a found count above 0.

editorial: The section heading credits the second value with the 39 of 39 join, but the post says the before/after was not shown. Setting this beside the docs' 'no restart' claim, the most valuable cross-node result is overstated in the heading. Fix: Rename the heading to 'With header propagation on, 39 of 39 traces joined across two nodes' until the default case is measured. Move the Amazon Linux 2023 result and the cross-node join up into the opening, since that is what the docs don't say.

claims.text: OBI is a beta feature in Splunk Observability Cloud
OBI runs as a DaemonSet and captures traces and request metrics with no code change or restart
The chart turns OBI on with obi.enabled=true
OBI's outgoing propagation is off by default
hostPID, hostNetwork and privileged are the chart's default, and the chart lists a reduced set of capabilities
The chart guide names Ubuntu as its tested OS
Proxies and load balancers can affect propagation
Async frameworks need checking on their own for context association
Splunk recommends combining OBI with language agents, and OBI skips processes that already have OpenTelemetry instrumentation
Reduced capabilities can affect Java agent injection into non-root JVMs
A language agent gives you the deepest detail and joins the JVM at startup, so the pods have to roll
Chart 0.164.0 ships the same OBI (lab README)

brief.reader: Platform engineer running Java services on EKS who wants a first service map before asking any team to change a deployment
brief.decision: Whether to turn on OBI through the Splunk OTel Collector chart as a first layer across a cluster, before rolling out language agents
brief.question: Can I get services that are already running on EKS onto the Splunk APM map without restarting a pod, and what do I get from it?
brief.takeaway: You can decide from measured numbers: what one Helm value puts on the map for running services, what it does to the pods, and whether traces across nodes need a second value.
brief.adds: Existing pages state that OBI needs no restart and list what it captures. This post measures it on EKS on Amazon Linux 2023: services on the map, each pod's UID and restart count before and after, whether one trace spans two nodes with and without propagation, the Java helper OBI loads, and the p95 latency added.
brief.open_question: With obi.enabled=true alone on chart 0.163.1, how many running services reach the Splunk APM map, how many pod restarts does it add, and how many services share one trace across two nodes with and without outgoing header propagation?
tradeoffs: OBI first for a broad map, or a language agent for deeper framework detail
A privileged DaemonSet with host PID and host network, or the chart's documented reduced capabilities
Every namespace by default, or a namespace filter
Outgoing header propagation on, or kept at its default
